newsitem.title: THAILAND: Finance One says position healthy.
newsitem.headline: Finance One says position healthy.

text.p: Finance One Plc on Tuesday detailed its financial positions to counter market rumours last week that it faced problems ranging from big loan defaults to heavy foreign exchange losses.
Finance One executive vice president Samran Kanokwattana told a news conference that his firm had hedged 97 percent of its $460 million outstanding foreign borrowing against foreign exchange losses.
He said the remaining three percent of uncovered loans were denominated in yen which, because of the currency's recent weekness, do not entail any foreign exchange risks.

Finance One president Pin Chakapak said his firm, Thailand's biggest finance company, had extended about 20 billion of its total 67 billion baht lending to the ailing Thai property sector at end-1996.
He said about 1.1 billion baht, or about five percent, of its property lending was classified as non-performing but the delinquent credits were backed by adequate collateral. He did not elaborate.

Pin said Finance One's non-performing loans rose to 4.8 percent of lending to all business sectors at end-1996 from 2.5 percent a year earlier. This was in line with a tougher time faced by the Thai financial sector.
Finance One shares closed one baht up at 32 on Tuesday against 108 baht on September 30, and 165 baht a year ago.
Samran told reporters that about 21 percent of Finance One's total lending went to the sluggish hire/purchase business, including personal consumer loans.
He said Finance One had also tapped another $162 million of foreign loans on behalf of its clients who agreed to absorb foreign exchange risks.
"Due to the safeguards that we took, we have no problem financing our own medium-term foreign borrowings," he said.
Samran also denied market talk that Paribas Bank planned to divest its 6.91 percent equity stake in Finance One.
He said Finance One's current 14 billion baht operating capital gives it a highly respectable 19.9 percent capital/risk assets ratio compared with a 7.5 percent minimum set by the Thai central bank.
